title: norite update --json
description:
The machine-readable output of `norite update status`, `check`, `apply`, `mode` and `channel` (M24): what the daemon knows about a newer release of the client, and what it will do about one.

Versioned source of truth (CLAUDE.md rule 15): a change to what these commands print ships with a change to this file in the same commit. Every field is always present.

Each command prints how things stand after it. `apply` prints the status as the daemon answered it, before it restarts as the new version: `available` is the version being installed, and a later `status` says whether it is on `trial` or was `rolled_back`. `norite update receipt` is the installer scripts' and prints nothing.

version.description: The version the running daemon is. `dev` for a build that is not a release.

mode.description: auto: a verified release is installed by itself. notify: the daemon checks and waits for `norite update apply`. off: nothing is checked unless asked.

channel.description: Whether alphas, betas and release candidates are offered. An install that is itself a pre-release is offered them unless told stable; any other, only when asked.

installs.description: Whether this daemon installs a release itself: only an install Norite's installer made, on a platform where it is done.

reason.description: Why it does not, when `installs` is false. Empty otherwise.

available.description: A newer version the last check chose, as SemVer without a leading v, or empty. It is one this install may move to: higher than what runs, on the channel, and one the signed-in instance talks to.

trial.description: A version installed and not yet confirmed, which is the one running, or empty. It is kept once it has stayed up; one that does not is undone.

rolled_back.description: A version that was installed, did not stay up and was undone, or empty. It is not installed again.

last_check.description: When the release listing was last read, RFC 3339 in UTC, or empty when it never was.

last_error.description: Why the last check or installation failed, or empty. A release whose signature did not verify is said here.
